newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $0.50-trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $0.50-trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices on Thursday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by sluggish pork demand, livestock dealers said.
The softer demand weighed on pork prices at midday and fueled speculation that packers would lower cash hog bids on Thursday as a result, to offset squeezed operating margins, they said.

Top prices for interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs delivered to the plant could range $47.00 to $48.00 and Illinois top prices for hogs at the plant could span $47.50 to $48.00, the dealers said.
Indiana and Ohio top prices for hogs at the plant door could range from $46.50 to $47.00, they said.
Midday pork prices overall were lower in light trading, which was attributed to retail interest being focused on beef for post-Easter advertising promotions, sources said.
Fresh loin prices were not fully established, hams were steady to $2.00 per cwt lower, lean trimmings were not tested and pork bellies were steady to $1.00 higher, USDA reported.
There were 24.25 loads of pork cuts and 1.0 load of trimmed or processed pork sold, USDA said.
